# The problem: Forage: a drone collecting decaying items on a battery

A drone works on a square area (coordinates in [0, 1]) for 100 time units. Items appear over time at random places. Each item has a value when it appears, and its value falls linearly at the item's own rate (value units per time unit); when the value reaches 0 the item disappears. The drone flies in straight lines at speed 1 (one distance unit per time unit) and collects an item by flying to it: it gains the item's value at the moment it arrives, and the item is gone. Only the target is collected (flying over other items does not collect them).

The battery holds 1.0 (full). Flying drains `drain` per unit of distance; nothing else drains it. The battery recharges only at the charger: when the drone arrives at the charger it charges to full at `charge_rate` per time unit (taking (1 - battery) / charge_rate time units, during which time passes as usual). The drone starts at the charger with a full battery. If the battery would run out during a flight, the drone stops where it ran out, is carried back to the charger (taking 2 time units), charged to full there (taking 1 / charge_rate), and a penalty of 40 is added to the cost; the item it was flying to is not collected.

One **decision** = choosing the drone's next target whenever it has arrived somewhere (or finished charging, or finished waiting). The **candidates** are every item visible now (appeared and not yet collected or disappeared), plus the charger. Choosing the charger flies there and charges to full; if the drone is already at the charger (it is then always full), choosing the charger means waiting there until the next item appears. Candidates come in a random order (reshuffled at every decision), so the position carries no information. When no item is visible the drone goes to the charger, or waits there for the next item, automatically. Nothing is known about items that have not appeared yet. A flight that arrives after the end collects nothing.

**Cost** of an instance (lower is better) = the value lost = the sum of every item's value at the moment it appeared, minus the values actually collected (so value that decayed before pickup, and items that disappeared or were left at the end, all count), plus 40 for every time the battery ran out. Families differ in where and when items appear, how values and decay rates are distributed, and the battery (drain, charge rate, charger position). Three training families: `scatter`, `hotspots`, `waves`; the test split adds a family that training never shows.

There is no known best solution: the score of an instance is **gap = 100 x cost / cost of Code Zero** on that instance, where Code Zero is the policy that always takes the first candidate (a random choice, because the order is shuffled). Code Zero scores 100; lower is better and nothing tells where the best possible lies (0 would mean losing no value at all).

# The problem: Forage: a drone collecting decaying items on a battery

A drone works on a square area (coordinates in [0, 1]) for 100 time units. Items appear over time at random places. Each item has a value when it appears, and its value falls linearly at the item's own rate (value units per time unit); when the value reaches 0 the item disappears. The drone flies in straight lines at speed 1 (one distance unit per time unit) and collects an item by flying to it: it gains the item's value at the moment it arrives, and the item is gone. Only the target is collected (flying over other items does not collect them).

The battery holds 1.0 (full). Flying drains `drain` per unit of distance; nothing else drains it. The battery recharges only at the charger: when the drone arrives at the charger it charges to full at `charge_rate` per time unit (taking (1 - battery) / charge_rate time units, during which time passes as usual). The drone starts at the charger with a full battery. If the battery would run out during a flight, the drone stops where it ran out, is carried back to the charger (taking 2 time units), charged to full there (taking 1 / charge_rate), and a penalty of 40 is added to the cost; the item it was flying to is not collected.

One **decision** = choosing the drone's next target whenever it has arrived somewhere (or finished charging, or finished waiting). The **candidates** are every item visible now (appeared and not yet collected or disappeared), plus the charger. Choosing the charger flies there and charges to full; if the drone is already at the charger (it is then always full), choosing the charger means waiting there until the next item appears. Candidates come in a random order (reshuffled at every decision), so the position carries no information. When no item is visible the drone goes to the charger, or waits there for the next item, automatically. Nothing is known about items that have not appeared yet. A flight that arrives after the end collects nothing.

**Cost** of an instance (lower is better) = the value lost = the sum of every item's value at the moment it appeared, minus the values actually collected (so value that decayed before pickup, and items that disappeared or were left at the end, all count), plus 40 for every time the battery ran out. Families differ in where and when items appear, how values and decay rates are distributed, and the battery (drain, charge rate, charger position). Three training families: `scatter`, `hotspots`, `waves`; the test split adds a family that training never shows.

There is no known best solution: the score of an instance is **gap = 100 x cost / cost of Code Zero** on that instance, where Code Zero is the policy that always takes the first candidate (a random choice, because the order is shuffled). Code Zero scores 100; lower is better and nothing tells where the best possible lies (0 would mean losing no value at all).

```python
    pos = np.asarray(pos, dtype=float)
    targets = np.asarray(targets, dtype=float)
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    rates = np.asarray(rates, dtype=float)
```

```python
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Directional alignment of each candidate with the recent arrival drift (wave front), scaled by surviving value; 0 for charger."""
    k = targets.shape[0]
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)

    if history is None or history.shape[0] == 0:
        return out

    t_app = history[:, 2]
    recent = history[t_app >= time - 12.0]
    older = history[(t_app >= time - 26.0) & (t_app < time - 12.0)]
    if recent.shape[0] < 2 or older.shape[0] < 2:
        return out

    c_r = recent[:, :2].mean(axis=0)
    c_o = older[:, :2].mean(axis=0)
    v = (c_r - c_o) / 14.0
    speed = float(np.hypot(v[0], v[1]))
    if speed < 0.005:
        return out
    u = v / speed

    rel = targets - c_r[None, :]
    dist = np.hypot(rel[:, 0], rel[:, 1])
    ahead = (rel @ u) / (dist + 0.25)
    ahead = np.clip(ahead, -1.0, 1.0)

    surv = np.clip(values - rates * dist, 0.0, None)

    is_item = values > 0
    if not np.any(is_item):
        return out
    max_surv = float(np.max(surv[is_item]))
    if max_surv <= 0.0:
        return out

    speed_term = np.clip(speed / 0.03, 0.0, 1.0)
    out = ahead * speed_term * (surv / max_surv)
    out = np.where(is_item, out, 0.0)
    out = np.clip(out, -1.0, 1.0)
    return out
```

If the battery would run out during a flight, the drone stops where it ran out, is carried back to the charger (taking 2 time units), charged to full there (taking 1 / charge_rate), and a penalty of 40 is added to the cost; the item it was flying to is not collected.

One **decision** = choosing the drone's next target whenever it has arrived somewhere (or finished charging, or finished waiting). The **candidates** are every item visible now (appeared and not yet collected or disappeared), plus the charger. Choosing the charger flies there and charges to full; if the drone is already at the charger (it is then always full), choosing the charger means waiting there until the next item appears. Candidates come in a random order (reshuffled at every decision), so the position carries no information. When no item is visible the drone goes to the charger, or waits there for the next item, automatically. Nothing is known about items that have not appeared yet. A flight that arrives after the end collects nothing.

**Cost** of an instance (lower is better) = the value lost = the sum of every item's value at the moment it appeared, minus the values actually collected (so value that decayed before pickup, and items that disappeared or were left at the end, all count), plus 40 for every time the battery ran out. Families differ in where and when items appear, how values and decay rates are distributed, and the battery (drain, charge rate, charger position). Three training families: `scatter`, `hotspots`, `waves`; the test split adds a family that training never shows.

There is no known best solution: the score of an instance is **gap = 100 x cost / cost of Code Zero** on that instance, where Code Zero is the policy that always takes the first candidate (a random choice, because the order is shuffled). Code Zero scores 100; lower is better and nothing tells where the best possible lies (0 would mean losing no value at all).

## How the policy works

priority(candidate) = w1 * feature1 + w2 * feature2 + ...; the highest priority wins; on a tie, the first candidate wins. With no features every candidate scores 0, so the first candidate always wins: that is **Code Zero**, the starting point (0% progress). An optimiser fits the weights, including their signs. A new feature is kept only if the policy does better with it than the same refit without it, on training instances *and* on separate validation instances, and the gain isn't already given by the kept features.

## How policies are scored

Per instance, the **gap** is how far the solution is above a reference (lower is better). The score is the mean gap over families. **Progress** is the share of the way from Code Zero (0%) to the best reachable (100%).

```python
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Three-hop greedy chain value density: value collected over a 3-item greedy chain plus return-and-recharge time, normalised across items."""
    k = targets.shape[0]
    is_item = values > 0
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)
    if not np.any(is_item):
        return out

    # pairwise distances
    diff = targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :]
    D = np.sqrt(np.sum(diff * diff, axis=2))  # (k,k)

    # start leg
    t = np.sqrt(np.sum((targets - pos) ** 2, axis=1))  # (k,)
    bat = battery - t * drain
    feasible_start = is_item & (bat >= 0) & (t * drain <= battery)

    V = np.clip(values - rates * t, 0.0, None)  # (k,)
    T = t.copy()
    cur = np.arange(k)
    alive = feasible_start.copy()

    item_mask = is_item

    for _ in range(2):
        # D[cur, j] for all starts i and candidates j
        Dcur = D[cur, :]  # (k,k)
        # gain for each j
        gain_j = np.clip(values[None, :] - rates[None, :] * (T[:, None] + Dcur), 0.0, None)  # (k,k)
        feasible = (bat[:, None] - Dcur * drain >= 0.0) & item_mask[None, :] & (np.arange(k)[None, :] != cur[:, None])
        score_j = gain_j / np.maximum(Dcur, 0.05)
        score_j = np.where(feasible & (gain_j > 0), score_j, -np.inf)
        best = np.argmax(score_j, axis=1)  # (k,)
        has = np.any(np.isfinite(score_j), axis=1) & alive

        # update for alive starts
        rows = np.arange(k)
        nb = best
        dstep = Dcur[rows, nb]
        gstep = gain_j[rows, nb]
        V = np.where(has, V + gstep, V)
        T = np.where(has, T + dstep, T)
        bat = np.where(has, bat - dstep * drain, bat)
        cur = np.where(has, nb, cur)
        alive = has

    # return-and-recharge leg
    dret = np.sqrt(np.sum((targets[cur] - charger) ** 2, axis=1))
    T = T + dret + (1.0 - np.clip(bat, 0.0, 1.0)) / max(charge_rate, 1e-6)

    raw = V / np.maximum(T, 0.2)
    raw = np.where(feasible_start, raw, 0.0)

    max_raw = np.max(raw[is_item]) if np.any(is_item) else 0.0
    if max_raw <= 0:
        return out
    out = np.clip(2.0 * (raw / max_raw - 0.5), -1.0, 1.0)
    out = np.where(feasible_start, out, 0.0)
    out = np.where(is_item, out, 0.0)
    return out
```

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Directional alignment of each candidate with the recent arrival drift (wave front), scaled by surviving value; 0 for charger."""
    k = targets.shape[0]
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)

    if history is None or history.shape[0] == 0:
        return out

    t_app = history[:, 2]
    recent = history[t_app >= time - 12.0]
    older = history[(t_app >= time - 26.0) & (t_app < time - 12.0)]
    if recent.shape[0] < 2 or older.shape[0] < 2:
        return out

    c_r = recent[:, :2].mean(axis=0)
    c_o = older[:, :2].mean(axis=0)
    v = (c_r - c_o) / 14.0
    speed = float(np.hypot(v[0], v[1]))
    if speed < 0.005:
        return out
    u = v / speed

    rel = targets - c_r[None, :]
    dist = np.hypot(rel[:, 0], rel[:, 1])
    ahead = (rel @ u) / (dist + 0.25)
    ahead = np.clip(ahead, -1.0, 1.0)

    surv = np.clip(values - rates * dist, 0.0, None)

    is_item = values > 0
    if not np.any(is_item):
        return out
    max_surv = float(np.max(surv[is_item]))
    if max_surv <= 0.0:
        return out

    speed_term = np.clip(speed / 0.03, 0.0, 1.0)
    out = ahead * speed_term * (surv / max_surv)
    out = np.where(is_item, out, 0.0)
    out = np.clip(out, -1.0, 1.0)
    return out

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Endgame sprint: one-way surviving value per distance (normalised), gated to the last charge-cycle window; charger row penalised by battery shortfall inside that window."""
    pos = np.asarray(pos, dtype=float)
    targets = np.asarray(targets, dtype=float)
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    rates = np.asarray(rates, dtype=float)

    gate = 1.0 if time_left <= (1.0 / max(charge_rate, 1e-6) + 3.0) else 0.0

    out = np.zeros(values.shape[0], dtype=float)
    if gate == 0.0:
        return out

    is_item = values > 0
    diff = targets - pos[None, :]
    d = np.sqrt(np.sum(diff * diff, axis=1))

    surv = np.clip(values - rates * d, 0.0, None)
    one_way = surv / np.maximum(d, 0.05)

    item_vals = np.where(is_item, one_way, 0.0)
    max_ow = np.max(item_vals) if item_vals.size > 0 else 0.0

    if max_ow > 0.0:
        norm = np.clip(item_vals / max_ow, 0.0, 1.0)
    else:
        norm = np.zeros_like(item_vals)

    out = np.where(is_item, norm * gate, 0.0)

    charger_mask = ~is_item
    shortfall = np.clip(3.0 * (1.0 - battery), 0.0, 1.0)
    out = np.where(charger_mask, -gate * shortfall, out)

    return out

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Rival-race margin: for each candidate, the drone's arrival lead over the fastest rival, weighted by the rival's surviving value, as a fraction of the candidate's arrival time; 0 for charger."""
    is_item = values > 0
    d = np.sqrt(np.sum((targets - pos[None, :]) ** 2, axis=1))          # (k,) drone -> cand
    diff = targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :]                    # (k,k,2)
    dd = np.sqrt(np.sum(diff ** 2, axis=2))                             # (k,k) cand i -> cand j

    # rival i flying to candidate j arrives at d_i + dd[i,j]; drone arrives at d_j
    arrive_rival = d[:, None] + dd                                       # (k rivals, k cands)
    lead = d[None, :] - arrive_rival                                     # >0 means drone beats rival i to j
    lead = np.clip(lead, 0.0, None)

    # weight each rival by the value it would still have on arrival at j
    rival_val = np.where(values[:, None] > 0,
                         np.clip(values[:, None] - rates[:, None] * arrive_rival, 0.0, None),
                         0.0)                                             # (k rivals, k cands)

    # only rivals that actually beat the drone (positive lead) matter; their held value is pressure
    contest = (lead * rival_val).sum(axis=0)                             # (k,)
    # normalise by the drone's own arrival time and the largest contest seen
    scale = np.max(np.abs(contest)) + 1e-9
    out = -contest / scale
    out = np.where(is_item, out, 0.0)
    return np.clip(out, -1.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Value density where the denominator is the *marginal* time the trip adds to the whole remaining schedule: time to reach the candidate, its expiry window, and the charge the trip forces — but only the charge that is actually needed before the next recharge, with a soft battery-feasibility gate instead of a hard one."""
    targets = np.asarray(targets, dtype=float)
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    rates = np.asarray(rates, dtype=float)
    pos = np.asarray(pos, dtype=float)
    charger = np.asarray(charger, dtype=float)

    is_item = values > 0
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    d_back = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)

    # value surviving the outbound flight
    val_after = np.clip(values - rates * d, 0.0, None)

    # how long until this item disappears on its own (inf for charger / non-decaying)
    tau = np.where(is_item, values / np.maximum(rates, 1e-9), np.inf)

    # soft feasibility: how much of the battery a one-way trip eats, squashed
    frac = np.clip(d * drain / np.maximum(battery, 1e-9), 0.0, None)
    feas = np.exp(-np.clip(frac - 1.0, 0.0, None) * 3.0)  # ~1 while reachable, decays once over budget

    # marginal charge cost: only the charge we must take *because* of this leg,
    # i.e. the shortfall between what we need for the round trip and what we have.
    roundtrip = d + d_back
    shortfall = np.clip(roundtrip * drain - battery, 0.0, None)
    t_charge = shortfall / max(charge_rate, 1e-6)

    # marginal time this candidate costs: outbound flight + forced recharge,
    # but an item that would vanish mid-flight contributes no denominator reward.
    denom = d + t_charge
    # if it expires before we get there, its "window" is the killer: scale down hard
    too_late = (d > tau).astype(float)
    denom = denom + tau * too_late  # inflate denominator for already-dead targets

    dens = np.where(is_item, val_after / np.maximum(denom, 1e-6), 0.0)
    dens = dens * feas

    # charger row: returning to charge is worth it when the world is decaying fast
    # and the battery is low; scale by the idle time we would spend charging back to full.
    world_decay = float(np.sum(rates[is_item])) if np.any(is_item) else 0.0
    t_idle = np.clip(1.0 - battery, 0.0, None) / max(charge_rate, 1e-6)
    d_ch = float(np.linalg.norm(charger - pos))
    charger_score = -world_decay * (d_ch + t_idle) * (1.0 - battery)
    out = np.where(is_item, dens, charger_score)

    scale = np.max(np.abs(out)) + 1e-9
    return out / scale
feature.measures: Value density where the denominator is the *marginal* time the trip adds to the whole remaining schedule: time to reach the candidate, its expiry window, and the charge the trip forces — but only the charge that is actually needed before the next recharge, with a soft battery-feasibility gate instead of a hard one.

feature.code:
import numpy as np
import math

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Local arrival opportunity cost but the arrival rate is measured per-direction (angular sector) from history, so the cost of a trip depends on whether the trip heads into a rich or empty region of the map."""
    win = max(time - 20.0, 0.0)
    hist = np.asarray(history, dtype=float) if history is not None else np.zeros((0, 5))
    if hist.shape[0] > 0:
        recent = hist[hist[:, 2] >= win]
        if recent.shape[0] == 0:
            recent = hist
    else:
        recent = hist

    d = np.sqrt(np.sum((targets - pos[None, :]) ** 2, axis=1))
    val_after = np.clip(values - rates * d, 0.0, None)

    # angular sector rate: for each candidate direction, sum recent arrival values whose bearing from the drone is within +-30 deg
    k = targets.shape[0]
    if recent.shape[0] == 0:
        lam_dir = np.zeros(k)
    else:
        vec = targets - pos[None, :]                       # (k,2)
        dn = np.maximum(d, 1e-6)
        ux = vec[:, 0] / dn
        uy = vec[:, 1] / dn
        hv = recent[:, :2] - pos[None, :]                  # (h,2)
        hn = np.linalg.norm(hv, axis=1)
        hn = np.maximum(hn, 1e-6)
        hx = hv[:, 0] / hn
        hy = hv[:, 1] / hn
        cosang = ux[:, None] * hx[None, :] + uy[:, None] * hy[None, :]   # (k,h)
        in_sector = cosang > math.cos(math.radians(30.0))
        wvals = recent[:, 3][None, :] * in_sector
        lam_dir = wvals.sum(axis=1)

    span = max(time - win, 1.0)
    # direction-aware opportunity cost: value on arrival minus what we forgo per unit trip into that sector
    net = (val_after - lam_dir * d / span) / np.maximum(np.maximum(np.abs(values), 1e-6), 1e-6)
    # shift by the global rate as a baseline so an item still gets credit when its sector is empty but the world is busy elsewhere
    global_lam = float(np.sum(recent[:, 3])) / span if recent.shape[0] > 0 else 0.0
    net = net - (global_lam * d / span) / np.maximum(np.maximum(np.abs(values), 1e-6), 1e-6)
    net = np.clip(net, -1.0, 1.0)
    out = np.where(values == 0, 0.0, net)
    return np.nan_to_num(out, nan=0.0, posinf=1.0, neginf=-1.0)
feature.measures: Local arrival opportunity cost but the arrival rate is measured per-direction (angular sector) from history, so the cost of a trip depends on whether the trip heads into a rich or empty region of the map.

feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Estimated value collected per unit of *battery*, where the denominator is the round-trip electrical cost and the numerator also credits the battery level we return with (charging overhead weighted by how scarce battery is)."""
    pos = np.asarray(pos, dtype=float)
    targets = np.asarray(targets, dtype=float)
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    rates = np.asarray(rates, dtype=float)
    charger = np.asarray(charger, dtype=float)

    is_item = values > 0.0
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    d_back = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)

    # Electrical cost of the whole loop through this candidate and home.
    trip = d + d_back
    elec = np.maximum(trip * drain, 1e-9)

    # Value surviving the outbound leg.
    val_after = np.clip(values - rates * d, 0.0, None)

    # How much battery is *left over* after the loop; a cheap loop keeps reserve
    # for the next sortie, a costly one forces a full recharge (time cost).
    reserve = np.clip(battery - trip * drain, 0.0, 1.0)

    # Bytes of battery is not free: charging adds time proportional to what we burned.
    recharge_time = (trip * drain) / max(charge_rate, 1e-6)

    # Effective worth: surviving value plus the option value of retained reserve
    # (scaled to value units by the item's own rate, i.e. what that reserve could
    # still buy before decaying), divided by electrical cost incl. recharge time.
    option = reserve * np.maximum(rates, 1e-6) * d
    denom = elec + recharge_time * drain * max(charge_rate, 1e-9) * 0.0 + recharge_time
    denom = np.maximum(denom, 1e-6)
    score = (val_after + option) / denom

    score = np.where(is_item, score, 0.0)
    # Charger row: fly home only when the loop we can still afford is short;
    # proxy with the electrical reserve deficit (negative => battery is a problem).
    deficit = np.clip(1.0 - battery - d_back * drain, -1.0, 1.0)
    score = np.where(is_item, score, -deficit)

    s = np.max(np.abs(score)) + 1e-9
    return score / s
feature.measures: Estimated value collected per unit of *battery*, where the denominator is the round-trip electrical cost and the numerator also credits the battery level we return with (charging overhead weighted by how scarce battery is).

feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Expected value density: value that survives the trip divided by the round-trip travel-plus-charge time cost, with charger row scored by idle-wait opportunity."""
    # distances from drone to each candidate
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    # time to reach each candidate
    t_go = d
    # value remaining on arrival (clipped at 0)
    val_after = np.clip(values - rates * t_go, 0.0, None)
    # battery needed and whether we can make it
    need = d * drain
    can = (need <= battery).astype(float)
    # time to fly back from candidate to charger plus recharge to full (approx)
    d_back = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)
    t_back = d_back
    # battery after flight: battery - need; recharge time to full
    batt_after = np.clip(battery - need, 0.0, 1.0)
    t_charge = (1.0 - batt_after) / max(charge_rate, 1e-6)
    # total cycle cost in time
    cycle = t_go + t_back + t_charge
    # density of surviving value per unit of cycle time
    is_item = (values > 0)
    dens = np.where(is_item, val_after / np.maximum(cycle, 1e-6), 0.0)
    dens = dens * can
    # charger row: prefer charging when battery low and no good item nearby
    charger_row = ~is_item
    # urgency of charging: low battery, small distance to charger
    charger_score = (1.0 - battery) * (1.0 - np.clip(d / np.maximum(time_left, 1e-6), 0.0, 1.0))
    dens = np.where(charger_row, charger_score, dens)
    # normalise to roughly [-1, 1]
    scale = np.max(np.abs(dens)) + 1e-9
    return dens / scale
feature.measures: Expected value density: value that survives the trip divided by the round-trip travel-plus-charge time cost, with charger row scored by idle-wait opportunity.

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Negative tanh of the recharge time forced by a round trip the battery cannot cover (0 for charger)."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos, axis=1)
    d_back = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger, axis=1)
    need = drain * (d + d_back)
    deficit_time = np.clip(need - battery, 0.0, None) / max(charge_rate, 1e-9)
    out = -np.tanh(deficit_time / 5.0)
    out = np.where(values > 0, out, 0.0)
    return out

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Competition-adjusted arrival value: surviving value minus the value better rivals will take first, divided by the candidate's own value, clipped; 0 for charger."""
    d = np.sqrt(np.sum((targets - pos[None, :]) ** 2, axis=1))
    is_item = values > 0
    val_after = np.clip(values - rates * d, 0.0, None)

    # How far is every candidate from every other candidate: who can beat whom to the punch
    diff = targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :]
    dd = np.sqrt(np.sum(diff ** 2, axis=2))  # (k, k)
    # rival i vs candidate j: rival's arrival time from drone is d_i; candidate j arrives at d_j
    # rival beats candidate j if d_i + dd[i, j] < d_j (rival gets there first) -- but only if rival survives
    rival_val_after = np.clip(values[None, :] - rates[None, :] * d[:, None], 0.0, None)  # (k rivals, k cands)
    arrive_rival_at_j = d[:, None] + dd  # (k rivals, k cands)
    beats = arrive_rival_at_j < d[None, :]  # rival reaches j before drone does
    # value that will be stolen from j by rivals (only items, and rivals that are items)
    stolen = np.where(beats & (values[:, None] > 0), rival_val_after, 0.0).sum(axis=0)

    scale = np.maximum(np.abs(values), 1e-6)
    net = (val_after - stolen) / scale
    net = np.clip(net, -1.0, 1.0)
    net = np.where(is_item, net, 0.0)
    return net
feature.measures: Competition-adjusted arrival value: surviving value minus the value better rivals will take first, divided by the candidate's own value, clipped; 0 for charger.

feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Value per unit of *remaining horizon* risk: surviving value divided by (trip time + time until item's own expiry), 0 for charger, charger row = idle decay rate of visible world scaled by battery slack."""
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    is_item = values > 0
    # time until each item's value hits zero (its natural death)
    tau = np.where(is_item, values / np.maximum(rates, 1e-9), np.inf)
    # time to arrive
    t_go = d
    # surviving value
    val_after = np.clip(values - rates * t_go, 0.0, None)
    # effective window: we must arrive before expiry, and the remaining horizon also matters
    window = np.minimum(tau, time_left)
    # pressure: value arriving per unit of the tightest window left
    press = np.where(is_item, val_after / np.maximum(window + t_go, 1e-6), 0.0)
    # penalise items we'd arrive after they vanish (val_after already 0), and horizon overrun
    press = np.where(t_go > tau, 0.0, press)
    # charger row: how fast the whole visible world is bleeding value while we sit and recharge
    # only attractive when battery is low (need to go), else idle waiting is costly
    world_decay = float(np.sum(rates[is_item]))
    d_ch = float(np.linalg.norm(charger - pos))
    t_charge = max(1.0 - battery, 0.0) / max(charge_rate, 1e-6)
    charger_val = -world_decay * (d_ch + t_charge) * (1.0 - battery)
    out = np.where(is_item, press, charger_val)
    s = np.max(np.abs(out)) + 1e-9
    return out / s
feature.measures: Value per unit of *remaining horizon* risk: surviving value divided by (trip time + time until item's own expiry), 0 for charger, charger row = idle decay rate of visible world scaled by battery slack.

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Relative density gain from chaining a nearby second item after each candidate, clipped to [-1,1]; 0 for charger."""
    pos = np.asarray(pos, dtype=float)
    targets = np.asarray(targets, dtype=float)
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    rates = np.asarray(rates, dtype=float)
    charger = np.asarray(charger, dtype=float)

    k = targets.shape[0]
    is_item = values > 0

    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)          # (k,)
    Dc = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)     # (k,)

    # single leg
    c1 = d + Dc + (d + Dc) * drain / max(charge_rate, 1e-6)
    V1 = np.maximum(values - rates * d, 0.0)
    D1 = V1 / np.maximum(c1, 1e-6)

    # pairwise distances between candidates
    diff = targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :]            # (k,k,2)
    Dm = np.linalg.norm(diff, axis=2)                           # (k,k)

    # two legs: i then j
    d_i = d[:, None]                                            # (k,1)
    Dc_j = Dc[None, :]                                          # (1,k)
    V2 = np.maximum(values[None, :] - rates[None, :] * (d_i + Dm), 0.0)   # (k,k)
    c2 = d_i + Dm + Dc_j + (d_i + Dm + Dc_j) * drain / max(charge_rate, 1e-6)
    D2 = (V1[:, None] + V2) / np.maximum(c2, 1e-6)              # (k,k)

    valid = is_item[:, None] & is_item[None, :] & (~np.eye(k, dtype=bool))
    best2 = np.where(valid, D2, -1.0).max(axis=1)               # (k,)
    has = valid.any(axis=1)

    out = np.clip((best2 - D1) / (best2 + D1 + 1e-6), -1.0, 1.0)
    return np.where(is_item & has, out, 0.0)

feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Opportunity cost of flying to each candidate measured only against the *best alternative* it displaces: surviving value minus the value of the strongest rival item the trip would cost, normalised, 0 for charger."""
    is_item = values > 0
    d = np.sqrt(np.sum((targets - pos[None, :]) ** 2, axis=1))
    # surviving value on arrival
    val_after = np.clip(values - rates * d, 0.0, None)
    # per-unit-time "worth" of each item: surviving value / arrival time (density proxy)
    worth = val_after / np.maximum(d, 1e-3)
    # best rival worth excluding self (only among items)
    worth_items = np.where(is_item, worth, -1.0)
    k = len(values)
    if k > 1:
        idx = np.argsort(-worth_items)
        best = worth_items[idx[0]]
        second = worth_items[idx[1]] if k > 1 else best
        # for each candidate, the best rival worth (if candidate is the top, use second best)
        is_top = worth_items >= best
        best_rival = np.where(is_top, second, best)
    else:
        best_rival = np.full(k, -1.0)
    # opportunity cost: what we forgo by choosing this candidate now, weighted by time spent
    forgone = np.clip(best_rival, 0.0, None) * d
    scale = max(float(np.max(values)), 1e-6)
    net = (val_after - forgone) / scale
    net = np.clip(net, -1.0, 1.0)
    net = np.where(is_item, net, 0.0)
    return net
feature.measures: Opportunity cost of flying to each candidate measured only against the *best alternative* it displaces: surviving value minus the value of the strongest rival item the trip would cost, normalised, 0 for charger.

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Rival-race margin: for each candidate, the drone's arrival lead over the fastest rival, weighted by the rival's surviving value, as a fraction of the candidate's arrival time; 0 for charger."""
    is_item = values > 0
    d = np.sqrt(np.sum((targets - pos[None, :]) ** 2, axis=1))          # (k,) drone -> cand
    diff = targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :]                    # (k,k,2)
    dd = np.sqrt(np.sum(diff ** 2, axis=2))                             # (k,k) cand i -> cand j

    # rival i flying to candidate j arrives at d_i + dd[i,j]; drone arrives at d_j
    arrive_rival = d[:, None] + dd                                       # (k rivals, k cands)
    lead = d[None, :] - arrive_rival                                     # >0 means drone beats rival i to j
    lead = np.clip(lead, 0.0, None)

    # weight each rival by the value it would still have on arrival at j
    rival_val = np.where(values[:, None] > 0,
                         np.clip(values[:, None] - rates[:, None] * arrive_rival, 0.0, None),
                         0.0)                                             # (k rivals, k cands)

    # only rivals that actually beat the drone (positive lead) matter; their held value is pressure
    contest = (lead * rival_val).sum(axis=0)                             # (k,)
    # normalise by the drone's own arrival time and the largest contest seen
    scale = np.max(np.abs(contest)) + 1e-9
    out = -contest / scale
    out = np.where(is_item, out, 0.0)
    return np.clip(out, -1.0, 1.0)
feature.measures: Rival-race margin: for each candidate, the drone's arrival lead over the fastest rival, weighted by the rival's surviving value, as a fraction of the candidate's arrival time; 0 for charger.

feature.name: marginal_cycle_time_density_with_soft_feasibilit
feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Value density where the denominator is the *marginal* time the trip adds to the whole remaining schedule: time to reach the candidate, its expiry window, and the charge the trip forces — but only the charge that is actually needed before the next recharge, with a soft battery-feasibility gate instead of a hard one."""
    targets = np.asarray(targets, dtype=float)
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    rates = np.asarray(rates, dtype=float)
    pos = np.asarray(pos, dtype=float)
    charger = np.asarray(charger, dtype=float)

    is_item = values > 0
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    d_back = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)

    # value surviving the outbound flight
    val_after = np.clip(values - rates * d, 0.0, None)

    # how long until this item disappears on its own (inf for charger / non-decaying)
    tau = np.where(is_item, values / np.maximum(rates, 1e-9), np.inf)

    # soft feasibility: how much of the battery a one-way trip eats, squashed
    frac = np.clip(d * drain / np.maximum(battery, 1e-9), 0.0, None)
    feas = np.exp(-np.clip(frac - 1.0, 0.0, None) * 3.0)  # ~1 while reachable, decays once over budget

    # marginal charge cost: only the charge we must take *because* of this leg,
    # i.e. the shortfall between what we need for the round trip and what we have.
    roundtrip = d + d_back
    shortfall = np.clip(roundtrip * drain - battery, 0.0, None)
    t_charge = shortfall / max(charge_rate, 1e-6)

    # marginal time this candidate costs: outbound flight + forced recharge,
    # but an item that would vanish mid-flight contributes no denominator reward.
    denom = d + t_charge
    # if it expires before we get there, its "window" is the killer: scale down hard
    too_late = (d > tau).astype(float)
    denom = denom + tau * too_late  # inflate denominator for already-dead targets

    dens = np.where(is_item, val_after / np.maximum(denom, 1e-6), 0.0)
    dens = dens * feas

    # charger row: returning to charge is worth it when the world is decaying fast
    # and the battery is low; scale by the idle time we would spend charging back to full.
    world_decay = float(np.sum(rates[is_item])) if np.any(is_item) else 0.0
    t_idle = np.clip(1.0 - battery, 0.0, None) / max(charge_rate, 1e-6)
    d_ch = float(np.linalg.norm(charger - pos))
    charger_score = -world_decay * (d_ch + t_idle) * (1.0 - battery)
    out = np.where(is_item, dens, charger_score)

    scale = np.max(np.abs(out)) + 1e-9
    return out / scale
feature.measures: Value density where the denominator is the *marginal* time the trip adds to the whole remaining schedule: time to reach the candidate, its expiry window, and the charge the trip forces — but only the charge that is actually needed before the next recharge, with a soft battery-feasibility gate instead of a hard one.

feature.name: directional_arrival_opportunity_cost
feature.code:
import numpy as np
import math

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Local arrival opportunity cost but the arrival rate is measured per-direction (angular sector) from history, so the cost of a trip depends on whether the trip heads into a rich or empty region of the map."""
    win = max(time - 20.0, 0.0)
    hist = np.asarray(history, dtype=float) if history is not None else np.zeros((0, 5))
    if hist.shape[0] > 0:
        recent = hist[hist[:, 2] >= win]
        if recent.shape[0] == 0:
            recent = hist
    else:
        recent = hist

    d = np.sqrt(np.sum((targets - pos[None, :]) ** 2, axis=1))
    val_after = np.clip(values - rates * d, 0.0, None)

    # angular sector rate: for each candidate direction, sum recent arrival values whose bearing from the drone is within +-30 deg
    k = targets.shape[0]
    if recent.shape[0] == 0:
        lam_dir = np.zeros(k)
    else:
        vec = targets - pos[None, :]                       # (k,2)
        dn = np.maximum(d, 1e-6)
        ux = vec[:, 0] / dn
        uy = vec[:, 1] / dn
        hv = recent[:, :2] - pos[None, :]                  # (h,2)
        hn = np.linalg.norm(hv, axis=1)
        hn = np.maximum(hn, 1e-6)
        hx = hv[:, 0] / hn
        hy = hv[:, 1] / hn
        cosang = ux[:, None] * hx[None, :] + uy[:, None] * hy[None, :]   # (k,h)
        in_sector = cosang > math.cos(math.radians(30.0))
        wvals = recent[:, 3][None, :] * in_sector
        lam_dir = wvals.sum(axis=1)

    span = max(time - win, 1.0)
    # direction-aware opportunity cost: value on arrival minus what we forgo per unit trip into that sector
    net = (val_after - lam_dir * d / span) / np.maximum(np.maximum(np.abs(values), 1e-6), 1e-6)
    # shift by the global rate as a baseline so an item still gets credit when its sector is empty but the world is busy elsewhere
    global_lam = float(np.sum(recent[:, 3])) / span if recent.shape[0] > 0 else 0.0
    net = net - (global_lam * d / span) / np.maximum(np.maximum(np.abs(values), 1e-6), 1e-6)
    net = np.clip(net, -1.0, 1.0)
    out = np.where(values == 0, 0.0, net)
    return np.nan_to_num(out, nan=0.0, posinf=1.0, neginf=-1.0)
feature.measures: Local arrival opportunity cost but the arrival rate is measured per-direction (angular sector) from history, so the cost of a trip depends on whether the trip heads into a rich or empty region of the map.

feature.name: battery_electrical_return_on_investment
feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Estimated value collected per unit of *battery*, where the denominator is the round-trip electrical cost and the numerator also credits the battery level we return with (charging overhead weighted by how scarce battery is)."""
    pos = np.asarray(pos, dtype=float)
    targets = np.asarray(targets, dtype=float)
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    rates = np.asarray(rates, dtype=float)
    charger = np.asarray(charger, dtype=float)

    is_item = values > 0.0
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    d_back = np.linalg.norm(targets - charger[None, :], axis=1)

    # Electrical cost of the whole loop through this candidate and home.
    trip = d + d_back
    elec = np.maximum(trip * drain, 1e-9)

    # Value surviving the outbound leg.
    val_after = np.clip(values - rates * d, 0.0, None)

    # How much battery is *left over* after the loop; a cheap loop keeps reserve
    # for the next sortie, a costly one forces a full recharge (time cost).
    reserve = np.clip(battery - trip * drain, 0.0, 1.0)

    # Bytes of battery is not free: charging adds time proportional to what we burned.
    recharge_time = (trip * drain) / max(charge_rate, 1e-6)

    # Effective worth: surviving value plus the option value of retained reserve
    # (scaled to value units by the item's own rate, i.e. what that reserve could
    # still buy before decaying), divided by electrical cost incl. recharge time.
    option = reserve * np.maximum(rates, 1e-6) * d
    denom = elec + recharge_time * drain * max(charge_rate, 1e-9) * 0.0 + recharge_time
    denom = np.maximum(denom, 1e-6)
    score = (val_after + option) / denom

    score = np.where(is_item, score, 0.0)
    # Charger row: fly home only when the loop we can still afford is short;
    # proxy with the electrical reserve deficit (negative => battery is a problem).
    deficit = np.clip(1.0 - battery - d_back * drain, -1.0, 1.0)
    score = np.where(is_item, score, -deficit)

    s = np.max(np.abs(score)) + 1e-9
    return score / s
feature.measures: Estimated value collected per unit of *battery*, where the denominator is the round-trip electrical cost and the numerator also credits the battery level we return with (charging overhead weighted by how scarce battery is).

feature.name: wave_front_alignment
feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Directional alignment of each candidate with the recent arrival drift (wave front), scaled by surviving value; 0 for charger."""
    k = targets.shape[0]
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)

    if history is None or history.shape[0] == 0:
        return out

    t_app = history[:, 2]
    recent = history[t_app >= time - 12.0]
    older = history[(t_app >= time - 26.0) & (t_app < time - 12.0)]
    if recent.shape[0] < 2 or older.shape[0] < 2:
        return out

    c_r = recent[:, :2].mean(axis=0)
    c_o = older[:, :2].mean(axis=0)
    v = (c_r - c_o) / 14.0
    speed = float(np.hypot(v[0], v[1]))
    if speed < 0.005:
        return out
    u = v / speed

    rel = targets - c_r[None, :]
    dist = np.hypot(rel[:, 0], rel[:, 1])
    ahead = (rel @ u) / (dist + 0.25)
    ahead = np.clip(ahead, -1.0, 1.0)

    surv = np.clip(values - rates * dist, 0.0, None)

    is_item = values > 0
    if not np.any(is_item):
        return out
    max_surv = float(np.max(surv[is_item]))
    if max_surv <= 0.0:
        return out

    speed_term = np.clip(speed / 0.03, 0.0, 1.0)
    out = ahead * speed_term * (surv / max_surv)
    out = np.where(is_item, out, 0.0)
    out = np.clip(out, -1.0, 1.0)
    return out

idea.hypothesis: Waves arrive as a moving front, so the drift direction of recent arrivals predicts where value will keep appearing. Items lying ahead of that drift are worth re-visiting/grabbing with slack; the champion has no directional signal and instead reacts item by item, which is why waves shows the lowest pickups (241) and the highest charger time (26.4%).

For each candidate: rel = target - c_r, dist = |rel|, ahead = (rel.u)/(dist+0.25) in [-1,1]. surv_i = clip(values - rates*|target-pos|, 0, None). out_i = ahead_i * clip(speed/0.03, 0, 1) * (surv_i / max over item candidates of surv). Set out = 0 for the charger row (values==0) and clip final to [-1,1].

import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Three-hop greedy chain value density: value collected over a 3-item greedy chain plus return-and-recharge time, normalised across items."""
    k = targets.shape[0]
    is_item = values > 0
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)
    if not np.any(is_item):
        return out

    # pairwise distances
    diff = targets[:, None, :] - targets[None, :, :]
    D = np.sqrt(np.sum(diff * diff, axis=2))  # (k,k)

    # start leg
    t = np.sqrt(np.sum((targets - pos) ** 2, axis=1))  # (k,)
    bat = battery - t * drain
    feasible_start = is_item & (bat >= 0) & (t * drain <= battery)

    V = np.clip(values - rates * t, 0.0, None)  # (k,)
    T = t.copy()
    cur = np.arange(k)
    alive = feasible_start.copy()

    item_mask = is_item

    for _ in range(2):
        # D[cur, j] for all starts i and candidates j
        Dcur = D[cur, :]  # (k,k)
        # gain for each j
        gain_j = np.clip(values[None, :] - rates[None, :] * (T[:, None] + Dcur), 0.0, None)  # (k,k)
        feasible = (bat[:, None] - Dcur * drain >= 0.0) & item_mask[None, :] & (np.arange(k)[None, :] != cur[:, None])
        score_j = gain_j / np.maximum(Dcur, 0.05)
        score_j = np.where(feasible & (gain_j > 0), score_j, -np.inf)
        best = np.argmax(score_j, axis=1)  # (k,)
        has = np.any(np.isfinite(score_j), axis=1) & alive

        # update for alive starts
        rows = np.arange(k)
        nb = best
        dstep = Dcur[rows, nb]
        gstep = gain_j[rows, nb]
        V = np.where(has, V + gstep, V)
        T = np.where(has, T + dstep, T)
        bat = np.where(has, bat - dstep * drain, bat)
        cur = np.where(has, nb, cur)
        alive = has

    # return-and-recharge leg
    dret = np.sqrt(np.sum((targets[cur] - charger) ** 2, axis=1))
    T = T + dret + (1.0 - np.clip(bat, 0.0, 1.0)) / max(charge_rate, 1e-6)

    raw = V / np.maximum(T, 0.2)
    raw = np.where(feasible_start, raw, 0.0)

    max_raw = np.max(raw[is_item]) if np.any(is_item) else 0.0
    if max_raw <= 0:
        return out
    out = np.clip(2.0 * (raw / max_raw - 0.5), -1.0, 1.0)
    out = np.where(feasible_start, out, 0.0)
    out = np.where(is_item, out, 0.0)
    return out

idea.hypothesis: The champion scores one item at a time plus one look-ahead step (f025), which is weighted almost nothing (importance 0.099). A battery-cycle-aware greedy chain of three items measures the real payoff of a trip; in sparse scatter/waves this is where the missed 35-40% is lost, because a single far item looks bad while a chain of three looks good.
idea.feature: Let is_item = values>0, D[i,j] = |targets[i]-targets[j]|. For every start i with is_item[i]: t = |targets[i]-pos|; bat = battery - t*drain; if bat < 0 or t*drain > battery, feature_i = 0. V = clip(values[i]-rates[i]*t,0,None); T = t; cur = i. Finally add the return-and-recharge leg: T += |targets[cur]-charger| + (1-clip(bat,0,1))/max(charge_rate,1e-6). raw_i = V/max(T, 0.2). Then normalise across item candidates: out_i = clip(2*(raw_i/max(raw_items) - 0.5), -1, 1); out = 0 for the charger row and for infeasible starts.

feature.name: endgame_stop_charging_sprint
feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """Endgame sprint: one-way surviving value per distance (normalised), gated to the last charge-cycle window; charger row penalised by battery shortfall inside that window."""
    pos = np.asarray(pos, dtype=float)
    targets = np.asarray(targets, dtype=float)
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    rates = np.asarray(rates, dtype=float)

    gate = 1.0 if time_left <= (1.0 / max(charge_rate, 1e-6) + 3.0) else 0.0

    out = np.zeros(values.shape[0], dtype=float)
    if gate == 0.0:
        return out

    is_item = values > 0
    diff = targets - pos[None, :]
    d = np.sqrt(np.sum(diff * diff, axis=1))

    surv = np.clip(values - rates * d, 0.0, None)
    one_way = surv / np.maximum(d, 0.05)

    item_vals = np.where(is_item, one_way, 0.0)
    max_ow = np.max(item_vals) if item_vals.size > 0 else 0.0

    if max_ow > 0.0:
        norm = np.clip(item_vals / max_ow, 0.0, 1.0)
    else:
        norm = np.zeros_like(item_vals)

    out = np.where(is_item, norm * gate, 0.0)

    charger_mask = ~is_item
    shortfall = np.clip(3.0 * (1.0 - battery), 0.0, 1.0)
    out = np.where(charger_mask, -gate * shortfall, out)

    return out

feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """s = 1 - ttl/time_left (clipped), times surviving value relative to the best surviving item value; 0 for charger."""
    is_item = values > 0
    safe_rates = np.maximum(rates, 1e-6)
    ttl = np.clip(values / safe_rates, 0.0, 1e6)
    frac = np.clip(ttl / max(time_left, 1.0), 0.0, 1.5)
    s = np.clip(1.0 - frac, -1.0, 1.0)
    dist = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    surv = np.clip(values - rates * dist, 0.0, None)
    surv_items = np.where(is_item, surv, 0.0)
    max_surv = np.max(surv_items) if surv_items.size else 0.0
    denom = max(max_surv, 1e-9)
    out = s * (surv / denom)
    out = np.where(is_item, out, 0.0)
    return np.clip(out, -1.0, 1.0)

system:
You are the **Navigator** in Helix, an evolutionary search. You don't write candidates. You keep the search oriented: you maintain a map of **approaches** (the different ways the incumbent could be improved) and decide where the effort goes next.

Two loops do the work. The **deep loop** (a Researcher, then Coders) runs experiments on the approaches you assign. The **wide loop** (a Mutator) makes undirected variations of whatever you hand it, and of nothing else: it never sees approaches or hypotheses, only artefacts and scores.

## The approach tree

Each approach has a state:
- `untried`: brainstormed, not tested yet;
- `promising`: something under it gained on validation. Gets the most effort, and is split into deeper sub-approaches;
- `unproven`: tried without a gain, but nothing shows it can't work. Retried occasionally, at lower priority. Bad scores are not proof;
- `pruned`: the engine verified a certificate that everything under it adds nothing. Never assigned again.

## Each generation, decide

1. **Brainstorm** new approaches when the map is thin or the promising ones are drying up. Make them genuinely different from each other, and add deeper sub-approaches under promising ones.
2. **Assign the Researcher** to approaches, each with a mode: `explore` (an untried approach), `exploit` (deepen a promising one), `probe` (a cheap experiment to learn whether an unproven one has anything).
3. **Hand the Mutator parents**: ids from the ledger to vary. The engine already gives two slots to the most important kept features (variants of kept features win far more often); you choose the rest. Spread those: width means variety across approaches. Near-misses and surprising scores are good parents.
4. **Combinations**: pairs of features that each gained on their own but weren't kept, to retry together (some things only help next to another). A pair with a member that showed no gain alone is skipped: in testing, such pairs never gained.
5. **Prune requests**: approaches you believe are dead. The Prover will try to certify it; only a verified certificate prunes.

Effort follows evidence, but keep a share for the unproven and the untried: a search that only exploits stops finding things.

## Reply format

Start with the JSON block, then at most 80 words on your reasoning.

```json
{"new_approaches": [{"title": "<short>", "description": "<one sentence>", "parent": "<approach id or empty>"}],
 "research": [{"approach": "<id, or the exact title of a new approach>", "mode": "explore | exploit | probe", "why": "<one line>"}],
 "mutate": {"vary": ["<id>", "..."], "fresh": <how many fresh slots>},
 "combine": [["<id>", "<id>"]],
 "prune": ["<approach id>"]}
```

## What a candidate is here: a feature

The incumbent is a policy, a weighted sum of features; approaches are kinds of measurements (what quantity, under which conditions). Mutator parents are feature ids.

# The problem: Forage: a drone collecting decaying items on a battery

A drone works on a square area (coordinates in [0, 1]) for 100 time units. Items appear over time at random places. Each item has a value when it appears, and its value falls linearly at the item's own rate (value units per time unit); when the value reaches 0 the item disappears. The drone flies in straight lines at speed 1 (one distance unit per time unit) and collects an item by flying to it: it gains the item's value at the moment it arrives, and the item is gone. Only the target is collected (flying over other items does not collect them).

The battery holds 1.0 (full). Flying drains `drain` per unit of distance; nothing else drains it. The battery recharges only at the charger: when the drone arrives at the charger it charges to full at `charge_rate` per time unit (taking (1 - battery) / charge_rate time units, during which time passes as usual). The drone starts at the charger with a full battery. If the battery would run out during a flight, the drone stops where it ran out, is carried back to the charger (taking 2 time units), charged to full there (taking 1 / charge_rate), and a penalty of 40 is added to the cost; the item it was flying to is not collected.

One **decision** = choosing the drone's next target whenever it has arrived somewhere (or finished charging, or finished waiting). The **candidates** are every item visible now (appeared and not yet collected or disappeared), plus the charger. Choosing the charger flies there and charges to full; if the drone is already at the charger (it is then always full), choosing the charger means waiting there until the next item appears. Candidates come in a random order (reshuffled at every decision), so the position carries no information. When no item is visible the drone goes to the charger, or waits there for the next item, automatically. Nothing is known about items that have not appeared yet. A flight that arrives after the end collects nothing.

**Cost** of an instance (lower is better) = the value lost = the sum of every item's value at the moment it appeared, minus the values actually collected (so value that decayed before pickup, and items that disappeared or were left at the end, all count), plus 40 for every time the battery ran out. Families differ in where and when items appear, how values and decay rates are distributed, and the battery (drain, charge rate, charger position). Three training families: `scatter`, `hotspots`, `waves`; the test split adds a family that training never shows.

There is no known best solution: the score of an instance is **gap = 100 x cost / cost of Code Zero** on that instance, where Code Zero is the policy that always takes the first candidate (a random choice, because the order is shuffled). Code Zero scores 100; lower is better and nothing tells where the best possible lies (0 would mean losing no value at all).

## A feature

```python
import numpy as np

def feature(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """One line: exactly what this measures."""
    ...
    return values   # one number per candidate
```

- `pos`: shape (2,), float: [x, y] of the drone now.
- `targets`: shape (k, 2), float: [x, y] of every candidate, in the (random) candidate order. The charger is one of the rows (at a random position); it is the row whose `values` is 0.
- `values`: shape (k,), float: the current value of each candidate item (always > 0 for an item); **0 for the charger**, so `values == 0` marks it.
- `rates`: shape (k,), float: how fast each item's value falls (value units per time unit; the item disappears after values / rates more time units); 0 for the charger.
- `battery`: float in [0, 1]: the battery left (1 = full).
- `drain`: float: battery used per unit of distance flown (a flight of length d needs d * drain).
- `charge_rate`: float: battery regained per time unit while charging at the charger.
- `charger`: shape (2,), float: [x, y] of the charger.
- `time`: float: the current time (from 0).
- `time_left`: float: time until the end.
- `history`: shape (s, 5), float: every item that has appeared so far (including those already collected or gone), in order of appearance: [x, y, time it appeared, value when it appeared, decay rate]. Nothing about items yet to appear.
- Return one finite number per candidate (shape (k,)), or a few columns (shape (k, c)). The highest-scoring candidate is the next target.
- Import only `numpy` and `math`. No state between calls, no randomness, don't modify the inputs, no Python loops over candidates when a vectorised form exists (features run thousands of times per evaluation). Guard every division and log.
- Return finite numbers, roughly in [-1, 1] (normalise; the optimiser rescales anyway).

## How the policy works

priority(candidate) = w1 * feature1 + w2 * feature2 + ...; the highest priority wins; on a tie, the first candidate wins. With no features every candidate scores 0, so the first candidate always wins: that is **Code Zero**, the starting point (0% progress). An optimiser fits the weights, including their signs. A new feature is kept only if the policy does better with it than the same refit without it, on training instances *and* on separate validation instances, and the gain isn't already given by the kept features.

## How policies are scored

Per instance, the **gap** is how far the solution is above a reference (lower is better). The score is the mean gap over families. **Progress** is the share of the way from Code Zero (0%) to the best reachable (100%).

# The problem: Forage: a drone collecting decaying items on a battery

A drone works on a square area (coordinates in [0, 1]) for 100 time units. Items appear over time at random places. Each item has a value when it appears, and its value falls linearly at the item's own rate (value units per time unit); when the value reaches 0 the item disappears. The drone flies in straight lines at speed 1 (one distance unit per time unit) and collects an item by flying to it: it gains the item's value at the moment it arrives, and the item is gone. Only the target is collected (flying over other items does not collect them).

The battery holds 1.0 (full). Flying drains `drain` per unit of distance; nothing else drains it. The battery recharges only at the charger: when the drone arrives at the charger it charges to full at `charge_rate` per time unit (taking (1 - battery) / charge_rate time units, during which time passes as usual). The drone starts at the charger with a full battery. If the battery would run out during a flight, the drone stops where it ran out, is carried back to the charger (taking 2 time units), charged to full there (taking 1 / charge_rate), and a penalty of 40 is added to the cost; the item it was flying to is not collected.

One **decision** = choosing the drone's next target whenever it has arrived somewhere (or finished charging, or finished waiting). The **candidates** are every item visible now (appeared and not yet collected or disappeared), plus the charger. Choosing the charger flies there and charges to full; if the drone is already at the charger (it is then always full), choosing the charger means waiting there until the next item appears. Candidates come in a random order (reshuffled at every decision), so the position carries no information. When no item is visible the drone goes to the charger, or waits there for the next item, automatically. Nothing is known about items that have not appeared yet. A flight that arrives after the end collects nothing.

**Cost** of an instance (lower is better) = the value lost = the sum of every item's value at the moment it appeared, minus the values actually collected (so value that decayed before pickup, and items that disappeared or were left at the end, all count), plus 40 for every time the battery ran out. Families differ in where and when items appear, how values and decay rates are distributed, and the battery (drain, charge rate, charger position). Three training families: `scatter`, `hotspots`, `waves`; the test split adds a family that training never shows.

There is no known best solution: the score of an instance is **gap = 100 x cost / cost of Code Zero** on that instance, where Code Zero is the policy that always takes the first candidate (a random choice, because the order is shuffled). Code Zero scores 100; lower is better and nothing tells where the best possible lies (0 would mean losing no value at all).

- `pos`: shape (2,), float: [x, y] of the drone now.
- `targets`: shape (k, 2), float: [x, y] of every candidate, in the (random) candidate order. The charger is one of the rows (at a random position); it is the row whose `values` is 0.
- `values`: shape (k,), float: the current value of each candidate item (always > 0 for an item); **0 for the charger**, so `values == 0` marks it.
- `rates`: shape (k,), float: how fast each item's value falls (value units per time unit; the item disappears after values / rates more time units); 0 for the charger.
- `battery`: float in [0, 1]: the battery left (1 = full).
- `drain`: float: battery used per unit of distance flown (a flight of length d needs d * drain).
- `charge_rate`: float: battery regained per time unit while charging at the charger.
- `charger`: shape (2,), float: [x, y] of the charger.
- `time`: float: the current time (from 0).
- `time_left`: float: time until the end.
- `history`: shape (s, 5), float: every item that has appeared so far (including those already collected or gone), in order of appearance: [x, y, time it appeared, value when it appeared, decay rate]. Nothing about items yet to appear.
- Return one finite number per candidate (shape (k,)), or a few columns (shape (k, c)). The highest-scoring candidate is the next target.
- Import only `numpy` and `math`. No state between calls, no randomness, don't modify the inputs, no Python loops over candidates when a vectorised form exists (features run thousands of times per evaluation). Guard every division and log.
- Return finite numbers, roughly in [-1, 1] (normalise; the optimiser rescales anyway).

## How the policy works

priority(candidate) = w1 * feature1 + w2 * feature2 + ...; the highest priority wins; on a tie, the first candidate wins. With no features every candidate scores 0, so the first candidate always wins: that is **Code Zero**, the starting point (0% progress). An optimiser fits the weights, including their signs. A new feature is kept only if the policy does better with it than the same refit without it, on training instances *and* on separate validation instances, and the gain isn't already given by the kept features.

## How policies are scored

Per instance, the **gap** is how far the solution is above a reference (lower is better). The score is the mean gap over families. **Progress** is the share of the way from Code Zero (0%) to the best reachable (100%).

# The problem: Forage: a drone collecting decaying items on a battery

A drone works on a square area (coordinates in [0, 1]) for 100 time units. Items appear over time at random places. Each item has a value when it appears, and its value falls linearly at the item's own rate (value units per time unit); when the value reaches 0 the item disappears. The drone flies in straight lines at speed 1 (one distance unit per time unit) and collects an item by flying to it: it gains the item's value at the moment it arrives, and the item is gone. Only the target is collected (flying over other items does not collect them).

The battery holds 1.0 (full). Flying drains `drain` per unit of distance; nothing else drains it. The battery recharges only at the charger: when the drone arrives at the charger it charges to full at `charge_rate` per time unit (taking (1 - battery) / charge_rate time units, during which time passes as usual). The drone starts at the charger with a full battery. If the battery would run out during a flight, the drone stops where it ran out, is carried back to the charger (taking 2 time units), charged to full there (taking 1 / charge_rate), and a penalty of 40 is added to the cost; the item it was flying to is not collected.

One **decision** = choosing the drone's next target whenever it has arrived somewhere (or finished charging, or finished waiting). The **candidates** are every item visible now (appeared and not yet collected or disappeared), plus the charger. Choosing the charger flies there and charges to full; if the drone is already at the charger (it is then always full), choosing the charger means waiting there until the next item appears. Candidates come in a random order (reshuffled at every decision), so the position carries no information. When no item is visible the drone goes to the charger, or waits there for the next item, automatically. Nothing is known about items that have not appeared yet. A flight that arrives after the end collects nothing.

**Cost** of an instance (lower is better) = the value lost = the sum of every item's value at the moment it appeared, minus the values actually collected (so value that decayed before pickup, and items that disappeared or were left at the end, all count), plus 40 for every time the battery ran out. Families differ in where and when items appear, how values and decay rates are distributed, and the battery (drain, charge rate, charger position). Three training families: `scatter`, `hotspots`, `waves`; the test split adds a family that training never shows.

There is no known best solution: the score of an instance is **gap = 100 x cost / cost of Code Zero** on that instance, where Code Zero is the policy that always takes the first candidate (a random choice, because the order is shuffled). Code Zero scores 100; lower is better and nothing tells where the best possible lies (0 would mean losing no value at all).

# The problem: Forage: a drone collecting decaying items on a battery

A drone works on a square area (coordinates in [0, 1]) for 100 time units. Items appear over time at random places. Each item has a value when it appears, and its value falls linearly at the item's own rate (value units per time unit); when the value reaches 0 the item disappears. The drone flies in straight lines at speed 1 (one distance unit per time unit) and collects an item by flying to it: it gains the item's value at the moment it arrives, and the item is gone. Only the target is collected (flying over other items does not collect them).

The battery holds 1.0 (full). Flying drains `drain` per unit of distance; nothing else drains it. The battery recharges only at the charger: when the drone arrives at the charger it charges to full at `charge_rate` per time unit (taking (1 - battery) / charge_rate time units, during which time passes as usual). The drone starts at the charger with a full battery. If the battery would run out during a flight, the drone stops where it ran out, is carried back to the charger (taking 2 time units), charged to full there (taking 1 / charge_rate), and a penalty of 40 is added to the cost; the item it was flying to is not collected.

One **decision** = choosing the drone's next target whenever it has arrived somewhere (or finished charging, or finished waiting). The **candidates** are every item visible now (appeared and not yet collected or disappeared), plus the charger. Choosing the charger flies there and charges to full; if the drone is already at the charger (it is then always full), choosing the charger means waiting there until the next item appears. Candidates come in a random order (reshuffled at every decision), so the position carries no information. When no item is visible the drone goes to the charger, or waits there for the next item, automatically. Nothing is known about items that have not appeared yet. A flight that arrives after the end collects nothing.

**Cost** of an instance (lower is better) = the value lost = the sum of every item's value at the moment it appeared, minus the values actually collected (so value that decayed before pickup, and items that disappeared or were left at the end, all count), plus 40 for every time the battery ran out. Families differ in where and when items appear, how values and decay rates are distributed, and the battery (drain, charge rate, charger position). Three training families: `scatter`, `hotspots`, `waves`; the test split adds a family that training never shows.

There is no known best solution: the score of an instance is **gap = 100 x cost / cost of Code Zero** on that instance, where Code Zero is the policy that always takes the first candidate (a random choice, because the order is shuffled). Code Zero scores 100; lower is better and nothing tells where the best possible lies (0 would mean losing no value at all).

# The problem: Forage: a drone collecting decaying items on a battery

A drone works on a square area (coordinates in [0, 1]) for 100 time units. Items appear over time at random places. Each item has a value when it appears, and its value falls linearly at the item's own rate (value units per time unit); when the value reaches 0 the item disappears. The drone flies in straight lines at speed 1 (one distance unit per time unit) and collects an item by flying to it: it gains the item's value at the moment it arrives, and the item is gone. Only the target is collected (flying over other items does not collect them).

The battery holds 1.0 (full). Flying drains `drain` per unit of distance; nothing else drains it. The battery recharges only at the charger: when the drone arrives at the charger it charges to full at `charge_rate` per time unit (taking (1 - battery) / charge_rate time units, during which time passes as usual). The drone starts at the charger with a full battery. If the battery would run out during a flight, the drone stops where it ran out, is carried back to the charger (taking 2 time units), charged to full there (taking 1 / charge_rate), and a penalty of 40 is added to the cost; the item it was flying to is not collected.

One **decision** = choosing the drone's next target whenever it has arrived somewhere (or finished charging, or finished waiting). The **candidates** are every item visible now (appeared and not yet collected or disappeared), plus the charger. Choosing the charger flies there and charges to full; if the drone is already at the charger (it is then always full), choosing the charger means waiting there until the next item appears. Candidates come in a random order (reshuffled at every decision), so the position carries no information. When no item is visible the drone goes to the charger, or waits there for the next item, automatically. Nothing is known about items that have not appeared yet. A flight that arrives after the end collects nothing.

**Cost** of an instance (lower is better) = the value lost = the sum of every item's value at the moment it appeared, minus the values actually collected (so value that decayed before pickup, and items that disappeared or were left at the end, all count), plus 40 for every time the battery ran out. Families differ in where and when items appear, how values and decay rates are distributed, and the battery (drain, charge rate, charger position). Three training families: `scatter`, `hotspots`, `waves`; the test split adds a family that training never shows.

There is no known best solution: the score of an instance is **gap = 100 x cost / cost of Code Zero** on that instance, where Code Zero is the policy that always takes the first candidate (a random choice, because the order is shuffled). Code Zero scores 100; lower is better and nothing tells where the best possible lies (0 would mean losing no value at all).

```python
import numpy as np
import math

def _f031_value_decay_acceleration_gradient(pos, targets, values, rates, battery, drain, charge_rate, charger, time, time_left, history):
    """For each item, the *marginal* value lost per unit of extra flight time relative to the value density already committed: how steeply value is bleeding off a candidate compared to what the drone is currently giving up by not switching, normalised to [-1,1]; 0 for charger."""
    is_item = values > 0
    k = targets.shape[0]
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros(0)
    d = np.linalg.norm(targets - pos[None, :], axis=1)
    # value surviving on arrival
    val_after = np.clip(values - rates * d, 0.0, None)
    # marginal loss rate per unit distance = decay rate (value lost per time = per distance at speed 1)
    # how much value the candidate is *still* losing once we arrive (residual bleed) vs its arrival value
    # residual bleed horizon: how long the item keeps decaying after arrival if we don't grab immediately
    # proxy: use the time_left to its own expiry bounded by remaining horizon
    tau = np.where(is_item, values / np.maximum(rates, 1e-9), 0.0)
    # fraction of the arrival value that will evaporate in the next unit of delay
    # = rate / val_after, but the item is gone once val_after hits 0
    fraction_bleeding = np.where(is_item & (val_after > 1e-9),
                                 np.minimum(rates / np.maximum(val_after, 1e-9), 1.0),
                                 0.0)
    # combine with arrival value so a high-value near-expiry item ranks above a slow bleeder
    # use the fraction of the candidate's *original* value that survives arrival times its bleed-rate
    surv_frac = np.where(is_item, val_after / np.maximum(values, 1e-9), 0.0)
    score = surv_frac * fraction_bleeding
    # charger row: prefer charging when battery is low and there is little value bleeding nearby
    charger_row = ~is_item
    # visible world's total bleed (value currently draining away per unit time)
    world_bleed = float(np.sum(rates[is_item]))
    # if world is bleeding fast, staying is expensive -> negative charger score when battery ok
    battery_slack = np.clip(battery, 0.0, 1.0)
    # charger should be attractive only when battery is low; scale by (1 - battery)
    charger_score = (1.0 - battery_slack) * (1.0 - np.clip(world_bleed, 0.0, 1.0))
    out = np.where(charger_row, charger_score, score)
    # rescale to roughly [-1,1]
    s = np.max(np.abs(out)) + 1e-9
    return out / s
```

# The problem: Forage: a drone collecting decaying items on a battery

A drone works on a square area (coordinates in [0, 1]) for 100 time units. Items appear over time at random places. Each item has a value when it appears, and its value falls linearly at the item's own rate (value units per time unit); when the value reaches 0 the item disappears. The drone flies in straight lines at speed 1 (one distance unit per time unit) and collects an item by flying to it: it gains the item's value at the moment it arrives, and the item is gone. Only the target is collected (flying over other items does not collect them).

The battery holds 1.0 (full). Flying drains `drain` per unit of distance; nothing else drains it. The battery recharges only at the charger: when the drone arrives at the charger it charges to full at `charge_rate` per time unit (taking (1 - battery) / charge_rate time units, during which time passes as usual). The drone starts at the charger with a full battery. If the battery would run out during a flight, the drone stops where it ran out, is carried back to the charger (taking 2 time units), charged to full there (taking 1 / charge_rate), and a penalty of 40 is added to the cost; the item it was flying to is not collected.

One **decision** = choosing the drone's next target whenever it has arrived somewhere (or finished charging, or finished waiting). The **candidates** are every item visible now (appeared and not yet collected or disappeared), plus the charger. Choosing the charger flies there and charges to full; if the drone is already at the charger (it is then always full), choosing the charger means waiting there until the next item appears. Candidates come in a random order (reshuffled at every decision), so the position carries no information. When no item is visible the drone goes to the charger, or waits there for the next item, automatically. Nothing is known about items that have not appeared yet. A flight that arrives after the end collects nothing.

**Cost** of an instance (lower is better) = the value lost = the sum of every item's value at the moment it appeared, minus the values actually collected (so value that decayed before pickup, and items that disappeared or were left at the end, all count), plus 40 for every time the battery ran out. Families differ in where and when items appear, how values and decay rates are distributed, and the battery (drain, charge rate, charger position). Three training families: `scatter`, `hotspots`, `waves`; the test split adds a family that training never shows.

There is no known best solution: the score of an instance is **gap = 100 x cost / cost of Code Zero** on that instance, where Code Zero is the policy that always takes the first candidate (a random choice, because the order is shuffled). Code Zero scores 100; lower is better and nothing tells where the best possible lies (0 would mean losing no value at all).
